title: The Queen's Gambit
description: The opening 1.d4 d5 2.c4. White offers a pawn to pull Black's centre pawn away from the middle, one of the oldest and most trusted ways to fight for the centre.

steps.instruction: You are White, so start the game by moving the pawn in front of your queen two squares forward.

hints.text: Your queen sits on d1. The pawn you want is directly in front of it.
Move the pawn from d2 to d4.

steps.explanation: This move is written 1.d4. The pawn takes a central square and stakes a claim in the middle of the board, the same idea as 1.e4 but on the queen's side. It also opens a line for your dark-squared bishop. Black replies 1...d5, matching you in the centre.

steps.instruction: Offer your c-pawn by advancing it two squares, alongside your pawn on d4.

hints.text: The pawn is on the queenside, next to your d-pawn. Push it as far as it will go on its first move.
Move the pawn from c2 to c4.

steps.explanation: This is the Queen's Gambit: 2.c4. You are offering the c-pawn, but it is not a true sacrifice. If Black takes with 2...dxc4, the pawn is awkward to hold and White wins it back later without trouble. The point is to tempt Black's d-pawn away from the centre, so your d-pawn is left unchallenged in the middle. Black often declines with 2...e6, guarding d5 and keeping the tension.

steps.instruction: Develop your queenside knight to the square that adds another attacker to d5.

hints.text: A knight belongs near the centre. From its starting square on b1, which move points it at Black's pawn on d5?
Move the knight from b1 to c3.

steps.explanation: 3.Nc3 develops a piece and adds to the pressure on d5. Now two white units, the c-pawn and the knight, bear down on Black's central pawn. Development follows the same rules whichever side of the board you play on: bring your pieces out, aim them at the centre, and prepare to castle your king to safety. The Queen's Gambit reaches those goals through the fight over d5.
